To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a systems biology approach was used to characterize the regulatory cascading of the gene regulatory networks controlling crown root formation downstream of CRL1 in rice.

we identified a gene regulatory network acting during crown root initiation in rice, and that we showed that this network links genes implicated in crown root development, in root meristems specification and maintenance, and in auxin signaling.
a gene regulatory network acting in the early steps of crown root formation was inferred and experimentally validated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the gene regulatory networks controlling the formation of crown roots (CRs).
the study of the molecular and genetic bases underlying the control of crown root development in rice.
the development of a systems biology approach that allows us to infer gene regulatory networks acting during crown root formation in rice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CRL1 dependent GRN is the first one that has been identified and characterized during the CR formation.
a systems biology approach was successfully used to infer the gene network controlling crown root initiation downstream of the transcription factor CROWN ROOTLESS 1.
the CRL1 gene regulatory network is a valuable source of information for understanding CR formation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have identified a network of genes involved in CR formation downstream of the CROWN ROOTLESS 1 (CRL) transcription factor and that this network is involved in auxin signal transduction, root meristem maintenance and specification.

we have inferred a gene regulatory network controlling crown root formation in rice and we have validated a regulatory cascade linking crown rootless1 to other transcription factors controlling crown root formation, root meristem specification, and auxin signalling.
we have inferred a gene regulatory network controlling crown root formation downstream of a key transcription factor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a systems biology approach based on a time series transcriptomic data set can be used to infer gene regulatory networks acting during a developmental process.
we have developed a method to infer a gene regulatory network in rice using a time series of RNA-seq data.
we have identified a regulatory cascade linking the transcriptional regulator CROWN ROOTLESS 1 to other genes controlling root meristem specification, crown root initiation or auxin signalization.
